newsitem.title: USA: Mercury cannot pay $17 mln in debt due. [CORRECTED 18:43 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mercury cannot pay $17 mln in debt due. [CORRECTED 18:43 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects debt total from $19 mln to $17 mln in headline and text.)
Mercury Finance Co said it cannot pay $17 million in commericial paper due Friday, because of downgrades in the company's debt ratings by Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's.
The consumer-finance company said it continues in discussions with its lenders to satisfy its working capital needs, but cannot predict the outcome of the discussions.
The company also said in a statement that it has retained the services of Salomon Brothers Inc to advise on all matters related to current and future capital needs, as well as all related issues.
Mercury said Wednesday it had to restate its earnings lower for the past four years by a total of about $90 million because of accounting irregularities.
Mercury said Wednesday the problems appeared to stem from unauthorized entries in financial records by its chief accounting officer, James Doyle.
But Doyle's lawyer reportedly accused Mercury of a charade and said Doyle was cooperating with federal authorities.

A special committee of Mercury's board, formed to investigate the accounting problems, has instructed its lawyers to contact Doyle's attorney, to attempt to reach Doyle, and to obtain information on the investigation, Lake Forest, Illinois-based Mercury said Friday.

The company has also directed its lawyers and accounting firm to expeditiously conduct and complete a thorough investigation of the auditing, accounting practices and procedures of the company and report to the Board, Mercury said.
Mercury shares have not traded on the New York Stock Exchange since they closed at 14-7/8 on Tuesday.
